The *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4) is a verse narrative located in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddakanikāya [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the spiritual career and past meritorious deeds of the elder Mahāmoggallāna. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text in five languages, but lists no curated cross-canonical parallels [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus demonstrate extensive shared material between this poem and other Pali texts, identifying 202 matching passages across 32 works [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual correspondence is with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo), comprising 41 matches and 9,223 shared characters, including a long continuous correspondence (§0.3–22.4 matching §5809–5852 at 0.92 similarity), alongside 49 matches with the first volume of the same commentary [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares recurring verse units with numerous other biographies in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Khadiravaniyarevatattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 11), *Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 20), *Sumaṅgalattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 22), *Rāhulattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 18), and *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3), as well as the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (highest score 85) and *Divyāvadāna*, as well as the Tibetan translation of the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka* (*Ārya-bodhisattvapiṭaka-nāma-mahāyānasūtra*) [DharmaNexus].
